thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate in us-west (3.4% over 5m). Paging oncall_jordan and SRE team. See runbook: https://redwood.ops/runbooks/5xx-spike

oncall_jordan: got the page, I’m online. looking at the dashboard now.

sre_lee: I’m on logs. early signs point to upstream gateway errors (502/504) from model-proxy instances hitting provider-x.

oncall_jordan: confirmed. spike started ~1929876400. rolling window 5m. Affected customers: small subset of Hosted API traffic to models/gpt-redwood-v2.

support_maya: support queue shows ~8 customer reports in last 10m, some mention timeouts and partial tokens. tagging them with incident label.

prod_emma: product — any config changes or rollouts in us-west in last 30m?

eng_miguel: no deploys reported. there was increased traffic from batch-worker via same route but below autoscale.

oncall_jordan: mitigation plan: 1) failover routing to us-east for new requests 2) increase model-proxy replicas in us-west 3) throttle large batch requests 4) open ticket with provider-x. doing 1 and 2 now.

observability-bot: action: started automated failover policy for /v1/generate to region us-east. (policy run id: pr-2049)

oncall_jordan: running k8s scale: `kubectl -n inference scale deploy/model-proxy --replicas=6` — starting to add capacity.

eng_miguel: pushed temporary rate-limit on batch-worker: `curl -XPOST https://api.redwood/infra/ratelimit -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","limit":80}'`

sre_lee: logs show many `upstream timeout` errors from provider-x: 504 in the proxy. excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:01Z proxy[proxy-3] ERROR upstream timeout id=abc123 path=/v1/generate status=504 latency=30000ms
2026-03-15T10:12:07Z proxy[proxy-2] ERROR gateway 502 provider-x service Unavailable
```

oncall_jordan: failover seems to reduce new errors after ~90s. still seeing backlog retries and some in-flight failures.

support_maya: raising CS priority. I’ve messaged affected customers with workaround: retry with region=us-east header.

prod_emma: coordinate on messaging — if we need public status update we should draft. customers on enterprise reserved capacity might be impacted, pinging account teams.

oncall_jordan: okay next steps: keep failover active, let proxies finish scale, open provider ticket, and start postmortem notes. I’ll hand off at the 30-min mark if stable.

observability-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: 5xx rate returned to baseline (0.4%) in us-west. auto-failover reverted.

oncall_jordan: marking incident as mitigated. creating incident ticket INC-4567 and recording timeline. please add any missing context.

sre_lee: quick root cause hypothesis: transient provider-x backend overload leading to elevated 502/504, our routing/auto-retry amplified visible 5xx rate. two things to address: upstream error detection vs transient retries, and alert noise from short-lived spikes.

eng_miguel: created provider ticket TRT-9982 and sent logs + p95 latency graphs. provider acknowledged possible internal flapping on their side.

prod_emma: thanks — we need to assess customer impact and decide if we publish a status page entry. support, please attach the list of affected accounts to INC-4567.

support_maya: done, attached 9 customers, including two enterprise accounts.

oncall_jordan: post-incident action items proposal (quick list):
- reduce alert flapping: change 5xx alert to a longer evaluation window and add a minimum error count threshold
- separate gateway upstream errors (502/504) from application 5xx so we can route alerts differently
- add dashboard panel for upstream provider errors and retry amplification
- add automatic cooling window to escalation (don’t page on 1m spikes)
- update runbook with provider escalation steps and per-customer mitigation examples

sre_lee: agreed. suggested Prometheus alert snippet for upstream-gateway errors:
```yaml
alert: UpstreamGatewayErrorSpike
expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",status=~"5..",upstream="provider-x"}[5m]))
  / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) > 0.02
for: 10m
annotations:
  summary: ">2% upstream 5xx on /v1/generate from provider-x for 10m"
```

oncall_jordan: two notes: 1) bump `for` to 10m to avoid immediate flips. 2) require at least 50 errors in window to avoid alerting on tiny traffic buckets.

eng_miguel: also add a separate alert for gateway 502/504 count that does NOT page but creates a dashboard ticket for SRE review:
```yaml
alert: ProviderXGatewayErrors
expr: increase(http_requests_total{upstream="provider-x",status=~"50[24]"}[5m]) > 20
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: warning
annotations:
  summary: "Provider-x gateway errors increased > 20 in 5m"
```

prod_emma: good split — pages only when it looks like real customer impact (>=2% errors AND p50 latency > 500ms). can we add latency gating?

observability-bot: sample combined rule suggestion: `((5xx_rate > 0.02 and error_count > 50) and latency_p50 > 0.5s) for 10m`

sre_lee: I’ll open a PR to update alerts and add the new grafana panel. will include a 15m cooldown after an alert before re-escalation.

oncall_jordan: runbook updates: add provider contact template, triage checklist (check retries, check for batch-job surges, check model-proxy queue depth), and customer notification template.

support_maya: I’ll update the support playbook with guidance for region failover advice and which customers to escalate to AE.

eng_miguel: for immediate deploy: PR #3145 will add the two alert rules and dashboard. target deploy after code review — ETA 3 hours.

prod_emma: assign post-incident review to weekly ops call. Jordan, Lee, Miguel, Maya on the ticket.

oncall_jordan: handoff time — I’m leaving the incident as mitigated, but watchlist remains until provider confirms root cause. handing to @sre_lee for overnight watch. I’ll post detailed timeline in INC-4567.

sre_lee: taking over. I’ll be available until 02:00 UTC. setting watch channel: #inc-4567-watch.

oncall_jordan: closing the page. thanks everyone for the quick turnaround :thumbsup:

observability-bot: NOTE: created ticket INC-4567, created PR 3145 (alerts/dashboard), linked provider ticket TRT-9982.

sre_lee: postmortem next steps (to add to INC-4567) — refine alert thresholds, add 10m evaluation, error_count floor 50, separate gateway vs app 5xx, add dashboard, and runbook updates. assigning owners in ticket.

prod_emma: agreed. add a short customer-facing snippet once provider confirms cause.

support_maya: will prepare messages and hold until provider confirmation.

oncall_jordan: thanks all. follow-ups in INC-4567.
